model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

equity_bridge.note: us-gaap:PreferredStockLiquidationPreferenceValue $21.2bn at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q; $20.1bn at 31 Dec 2025, new series issued in Q2 2026); dividends ~$1.2bn/yr (FY2025 1,099; H1 2026 584). Deducted at liquidation value because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 29,131 (COVID CECL build); FY2021 48,334 (reserve release); FY2022 37,676; FY2023 49,552 (First Republic from May 2023); FY2024 58,471 (incl. ~$7.9bn Visa gain); FY2025 57,048 (SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss). Revenue (NII + noninterest income = us-gaap:Revenues): FY2020 119,951; FY2022 128,695; FY2023 158,104; FY2025 182,447. Diluted EPS FY2020 8.88, FY2022 12.10, FY2025 20.02. The 3-year windows (FY2022-25) start from the FY2022 trough (rate-shock markdowns, no reserve release) and include the First Republic acquisition and the 2022-24 rate rise, so they overstate organic growth; the 5-year windows start from the FY2020 provisioning trough. Neither is a forward rate.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (4.0% FY27-29 tapering to 2.5%), anchored on nominal GDP plus ~1pp of deposit/IB/wealth share gain, off an FY2026E base that already embeds the 2022-26 rate reset and First Republic. The historical revenue CAGRs (12.3%/8.8%) are not repeatable: they are the zero-to-4.5% Fed cycle plus an acquisition. Equity CAGRs (5.3-7.4%) understate earnings growth because ~85% of earnings are distributed.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3/5-year CAGRs (7.4%/5.3%) diverge >30% from revenue (12.3%/8.8%) and EPS (18.3%/17.7%): JPM returns ~85% of earnings through dividends and buybacks (FY2025 $48.2bn on $57.0bn net income) and its stated equity swings with AOCI, so book value compounding does not describe per-share earnings power; EPS also benefits from a share count falling ~2-3%/yr. Growth is taken from the revenue series and guidance, and the equity CAGR is not used.

scenario_narratives.base: JPMorgan compounds revenue at ~4% off an FY2026 base that already embeds the 2022-26 rate reset, First Republic and a record trading half, with the efficiency ratio holding ~53% as AI savings offset a ~$20bn tech budget and volume-driven compensation, and provisions normalising from a light FY2026 to ~7% of revenue. GAAP EPS reaches ~$25 in FY2027 and ~$36 by FY2031; ~82-89% of earnings are distributed through the $6.60 dividend and $35-40bn/yr of buybacks. At a 10% cost of equity and a ~22% return on tangible common equity the franchise is worth ~2.6x tangible book, against the ~3.0x the market pays after the Q2 2026 record.
scenario_narratives.bull: The capital-markets cycle runs for years, JPM's IB and markets share keeps rising, NII compounds 5-6% on deposit share gains, and the AI programme delivers the guided ~10% headcount reduction, taking the efficiency ratio to 50%. ROTCE holds ~24-25% (the FY2024-26 run-rate) rather than reverting to the 17% through-cycle target, FY2028 EPS clears $30, and the Basel III final rule leaves the ~$50bn excess CET1 surplus, so the ~3x TBV multiple is sustained.
scenario_narratives.bear: Elevated asset prices and the 'increasingly complex set of risks' Dimon flags resolve into a market correction and a mid-sized credit cycle in FY2027-28: markets revenue falls ~20% from a record, IB fees ~25%, card net charge-offs return to 3.6-3.9%, and the first real private-credit/NBFI losses land after Tricolor and First Brands. Costs are not cut, provisions peak at ~$26bn, EPS troughs near $18, and Basel III Endgame's ~4% RWA uplift for JPM absorbs capital that would otherwise fund buybacks. ROTCE troughs at ~17%, still above the cost of equity, so the franchise remains worth well above tangible book but far below today's price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity - never on statutory operating cash flow (which is trading, loan and deposit movement) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at NPAT x g/ROTE is the reinvestment; preferred stock is deducted at liquidation value so the common claim is valued; 10% is the return an owner requires from a ~13x-levered G-SIB with the most cyclical fee line in US banking. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a ~22% return on tangible common equity and 2.5% growth the franchise is worth ~2.6x tangible book, so the ~3.0x the market pays after the Q2 2026 record embeds either a sustained ~25% ROTCE (the FY2024-26 run-rate, not the 17% through-cycle target management still guides to) or a cost of equity below 9%. Value the underlying: the Q2 2026 'record' includes ~$6.4bn of one-off other income and a record trading quarter, neither of which is in the FY0 base.
key_risks_to_valuation: Markets and IB revenue: ~$45bn of the FY2026E base is trading and investment banking; a 20% reversion is ~$9bn of revenue (~4.4%) and, against a fixed cost base, ~10% of pre-tax income
Credit cycle: every 100bp on the provision rate over ~$204bn of revenue is ~$2bn pre-tax (~3% of NPAT); a FY2020-style build (~14.6% of revenue) would halve one year's earnings
Net interest income: the ~$105.5bn FY2026 managed guide is 'market dependent'; every 25bp of deposit-beta or curve shift on ~$3.5tn of interest-earning assets is ~$2-4bn of NII (~2-4% of revenue)
Efficiency: the base assumes ~53% holds as AI savings offset ~$20bn of tech spend; every 1pp of efficiency ratio is ~$2.1bn pre-tax (~3% of NPAT)
Capital: the ~$45-55bn excess CET1 is unmodelled upside (~$17-20/share) if the Basel III Endgame final rule leaves it surplus, and a retention drag if JPM's expected ~4% RWA uplift is the outcome
Share count: the ~21m Q3 2026 repurchase estimate and the ~4m dilutive-award count are approximations until the Q3 10-Q cover prints; each 25m shares is ~1% of value per share

Terminal value carries a large share of value at a 10% cost of equity; the cap (15x FCFE, ~12.8x earnings) is not binding in the base (Gordon at 2.5% gives 13.7x), so the sensitivity grid is the honest range

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 279.1-366.5.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000019617) for FY2018-FY2025 annual NII, noninterest income, noninterest expense, provision, pretax income, income tax, net income, diluted EPS, equity, goodwill, intangibles, preferred stock, dividends, repurchases and share counts, and for the Q2 2026 10-Q (accession 0001628280-26-054343, filed 2026-08-06) income statement, balance sheet, share-based compensation, repurchases, diluted/basic shares and cover-page share count; JPM_Metrics.csv / JPM.duckdb (93 periods) for the reported history and kpis (buybacks, cash taxes, securities interest income). The quarterly CSV Revenue rows are an ASC-606 fee subset and were not used.
data_sources.qualitative: JPM_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): segments and revenue mix, Q2 2026 results and guidance (NII ~$105.5bn, adjusted expense ~$107.5bn, card NCO ~3.2%, CET1 14.1%/14.2%, $1.65 dividend, $50bn buyback), Basel III Endgame re-proposal and JPM's expected ~4% RWA increase, AI programme (~$2bn savings, ~10% headcount over five years), private-credit/NBFI exposure (Tricolor, First Brands), Dimon's macro warnings, competitive position, bull/bear cases.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E UNDERLYING total net revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP reported basis, not the FTE-adjusted 'managed' basis the company headlines, which runs ~$2-3bn/yr higher). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported. Build: H1 2026 actual 107,183 (NII 50,877 + noninterest income 56,306, Q2 2026 10-Q, us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet + NoninterestIncome) LESS ~6,000 of non-recurring gain sitting in Q2 2026 us-gaap:NoninterestIncomeOther (7,549 vs 1,154 in Q2 2025 and ~1.2-1.5bn/quarter normally; trading +1.9bn and IB +0.7bn YoY explain only a quarter of the +10.1bn YoY fee jump) = ~101,200 underlying H1; PLUS H2 2026 at NII ~52,500 (26.0 + 26.5/quarter, consistent with the raised ~$105.5bn managed FY guide less the FTE gross-up, Q2 ran 25,511) and noninterest income ~51,000 (~25.5/quarter: Q1 2026 24,470; Q2 2026 ex-gain ~25,400) = ~103,500. FY2026E underlying = ~204,700 (reported will print ~211bn). FY2025 actual 182,447 (NII 95,443 + noninterest income 87,004 = us-gaap:Revenues 182,447, 10-K); FY2024 177,556 incl. the ~$7.9bn Visa share gain. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027, one year from the valuation date as the engine's end-of-year discounting requires. The CSV Revenue column is correct on annual rows (it is us-gaap:Revenues) but the quarterly/half-year rows (e.g. Q2 2026 1,207) are an ASC-606 fee subset and are NOT bank revenue; every quarterly figure here is NII + noninterest income from companyfacts.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,658.2m common shares outstanding at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding 2,658,186,195) PLUS ~4m dilutive awards (Q2 2026 diluted weighted average 2,694.2m vs basic 2,689.9m) LESS an ESTIMATED ~21m shares repurchased in Q3 2026 (~$7bn at ~$330, the H1 2026 pace of $7.5bn/quarter: $8,325m Q1, $6,788m Q2, under the new $50bn authorisation) = ~2,641m fully diluted at the valuation date. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation ($2,340m H1 2026) is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; the buyback is a distribution of the FCFE the model capitalises, not a separate driver. REFRESH from the Q3 2026 10-Q cover (results ~14 Oct 2026, 10-Q early Nov 2026).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. JPMorgan is a Fed-regulated bank holding company: deposits (~$2.6tn), long-term debt (~$450bn), fed funds/repo and trading liabilities are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income, and cash and deposits with banks are held against that funding and are not surplus. The CSV total_debt/cash columns are null for JPM and are recorded here as 0 for audit; nothing is deducted or added. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the ~13-14% CET1 the firm runs) at the cost of equity. Preferred stock ($21.2bn liquidation preference at 30 Jun 2026, ~$1.2bn/yr of dividends) is a claim senior to common and is deducted at liquidation value in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E underlying FCFE = GAAP net income ~67,400 (underlying revenue 204,700 - noninterest expense ~108,000 (H1 actual 54,166 + H2 ~53,800; adjusted-expense guide ~$107.5bn managed) - provision ~10,800 (H1 actual 5,022 + H2 ~5,800) = pretax ~85,900 x (1 - 21.5%)) LESS capital retained ~12,200 (~4% RWA growth x ~$303bn CET1 capital, i.e. NPAT x g/ROTE). Reported FY2026 net income will print ~72bn (H1 actual 37,649 includes the ~$5bn after-tax Q2 gain). Cross-check on distributions: FY2025 common dividends 16,625 + buybacks 31,591 = 48,216 = 85% of 57,048 GAAP net income with CET1 drifting from 15.7% to 14.1%; FY2026E modelled distribution 55,200/67,400 = 82%. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 -147,782; FY2024 -42,012; FY2022 +107,119) is trading-asset, loan and deposit movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV OperatingCashFlow/FreeCashFlow columns are NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge (55,200 + 4,100).
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back: H1 2026 $2,340m (Q2 2026 10-Q) -> ~$4.1bn FY2026E (H1 is seasonally heavier: FY2025 3,614 on H1 2,012; FY2024 3,504; FY2023 3,117). ~2.0% of revenue. No separate net-share-settlement tax line is tagged; taxes withheld on vesting are immaterial relative to SBC at JPM's scale. SBC is already inside noninterest expense and therefore inside GAAP net income; the engine's separate sbc line is fed by adding it back into the ebitda_margin_path so it is charged exactly once.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income (~$190bn gross, $95.4bn net in FY2025) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction). The kpis interest_income series (FY2025 28,032) is investment-securities interest, a component of NII, not surplus-cash interest.
inputs.buyback_note: PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $15,113m in H1 2026 ($8,325m Q1, $6,788m Q2); FY2025 $31,591m; FY2024 $18,830m; FY2023 $9,824m. New $50bn authorisation announced June 2026 after the Fed stress test, alongside the dividend raised to $1.65/quarter from $1.50. The flat share count is fully funded: JPM repurchases ~2-3% of its shares a year against ~0.15% of SBC dilution. Buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover count, plus dilutive awards, less estimated Q3 2026 repurchases)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total stockholders' equity $374,598m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q) less preferred stock $21,200m (liquidation preference), goodwill $52,711m and other intangibles ~$1,300m (FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsNet, 31 Dec 2025; MSRs of $9,156m are NOT deducted, consistent with the company's TBVPS definition) = tangible common equity ~$299,400m = ~$112.6/share on 2,658.2m cover shares (company-reported TBVPS is on the same definition). Price is ~3.0x TBV and ~2.5x stated BVPS (~$133). CET1 capital ~$303bn, Standardized CET1 14.1% / Advanced 14.2% at Q2 2026 against a ~11.5% requirement incl. buffers, i.e. ~$45-55bn of excess capital that management is holding partly against Basel III Endgame uncertainty (JPM expects a ~4% RWA increase under the March 2026 re-proposal even as peers get relief). That excess is NOT added to the equity bridge and NOT released through lower retention; it is ~$17-20/share of unmodelled upside that would be recognised if the final rule leaves it surplus. ROTCE: FY2025 GAAP ~20% (57,048 - 1,099 preferred on ~$280bn average TCE); FY2027 base ~22%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year US Treasury ~4.5% (late September 2026) + beta 1.1 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 10.0%. Beta 1.1 is the measured five-year range (1.0-1.2) for JPM, below the 1.2 used for HBAN (a NIM-geared super-regional whose deposits proved flight-prone in March 2023) and above the 1.0 used for NAB.AX: JPM is the G-SIB that RECEIVES the flight-to-quality deposits and earns ~45% of revenue from fees, but it carries a ~$5tn balance sheet at ~13x leverage on tangible equity and its markets/IB revenue is the most cyclical line in the group. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, capital-markets and Basel III risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium. Residual-income cross-check at this rate: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (22 - 2.5)/(10 - 2.5) = 2.6x on ~$112.6 TBVPS = ~$293, which the engine base should approximate; the market's ~3.0x TBV implies either a sustained ROTCE of ~25% at a 10% cost of equity or a ~8.9% cost of equity at a 22% ROTCE.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branch and office network) are immaterial relative to $375bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests. Preferred stock is the only senior equity claim and is deducted at liquidation preference in equity_bridge (see funding_note), so the 21.5% cash-tax-rate driver is pure income tax (FY2025 effective 21.4%; FY2024 22.1%; H1 2026 21.6%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (house precedent HBAN 2026-09-29, NAB.AX 2026-09-24, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE)), and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. Owner-FCF is NOT used: statutory OCF is loan/deposit/trading movement (FY2025 -147.8bn) and deposits are not net debt. BVPS-compounding is NOT used: JPM distributes ~85% of earnings, so book value compounds at ~5-7% while earnings power compounds at 12-18%, and stated equity swings with AOCI. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue (FY2026E underlying: 204,700 - 108,000 - 10,800 = 85,900 = 42.0% + 2.0% SBC = 44.0%; history GAAP pre-tax: FY2018 37.5%, FY2019 38.8%, FY2020 29.9% (COVID CECL build), FY2021 49.0% (reserve release), FY2022 35.9%, FY2023 39.0% (First Republic bargain-purchase gain), FY2024 42.3% (Visa gain; ~39.6% ex), FY2025 39.8%; mid-cycle ex-one-offs ~39%); sbc_pct_path = 2.0%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation and software amortisation are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank, not add-backs); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the ~13-14% CET1 the firm runs = CET1 capital/revenue (~1.45x) x RWA growth, i.e. NPAT margin x g / ROTE; cash_tax_rate_path = 21.5% income tax; wacc = cost of equity 10.0%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -21,200 preferred stock. FY2027 base reconciliation: 204,700 x 1.04 = 212,900 revenue x (42.5% - 2.0%) x (1 - 21.5%) = 67,700 GAAP net income, less ~1,200 preferred dividends = 66,500 to common / ~2,641m = ~$25.2 GAAP EPS (FY2025 actual $20.02 diluted; FY2026E reported ~$26.4 incl. the Q2 gain, ~$24.5 underlying). Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) is unreported; 30 Jun 2026 is the latest balance sheet. Price is the NYSE regular close on 28 Sep 2026, not an after-hours print. The Analysis JSON attributes the Q2 2026 record entirely to trading; the XBRL shows ~$6.4bn of it in NoninterestIncomeOther, which this model treats as non-recurring.

bear.growth_rationale: The correction Dimon keeps warning about arrives: equity and credit markets reprice, markets revenue falls ~20% from the FY2026 record and IB fees ~25% (FY2022 precedent: revenue ex-NII fell 10% and pretax margin 36%), NII is flat as the Fed cuts into a slowdown and deposit costs lag, card and wealth fees stall. Revenue -3% FY27, flat FY28, then 2-3% nominal.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 56.0% (revenue falls against a cost base guided up to ~$108bn, tech/AI spend is not cut) - provision 8.0% (~16bn; card NCOs back to 3.6-3.9%, first private-credit/NBFI losses after Tricolor and First Brands) + 2.0 = 38.0. FY28 credit cycle: provision 13.0% (~26bn, about 1.2% of loans, below the FY2020 17.5bn = 14.6% of a much smaller revenue base, so a mid-sized cycle, not a crisis) with efficiency 56.0%: 33.0. Recovers to provision 8.0% and efficiency 55.5%: 38.5, held - AI savings absorbed by remediation, litigation and Basel III compliance; no operating leverage. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$21.4, FY28 ~$18.4; ROTCE ~17-18% in the trough, still above the cost of equity.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention held at 4.5-5.0% of revenue through FY27-29 despite -3% to +2.5% revenue growth because RWA migration in a downturn and the ~4% RWA uplift JPM expects from the Basel III Endgame final rule (late 2026, effective 2027) consume capital the model must top up; buybacks are cut, not halted (the 2020 precedent was a one-quarter suspension). Terminal 2% growth retains 2.9%.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenue off the UNDERLYING FY2026E base (204.7bn, ex the Q2 2026 gain). FY27 +4%: NII +4-5% (loan growth mid-single-digit, deposit share gains, securities reinvestment at higher yields offsetting modest Fed easing; the company's own ~$105.5bn FY26 managed NII guide is 'market dependent'), markets/IB flat-to-down from a record H1 2026 (Q2 trading 9.0bn vs 7.1bn a year earlier), asset management and card fees +6-8%. Held at 4% through FY29, tapering to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP; JPM already has ~12% of US deposits and ~8-9% of global IB fees, so share gains slow). 10-year average 3.3%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY27 42.5% = pretax 40.5% + 2.0 SBC: efficiency ratio 53.0% (FY2025 GAAP 52.4%; FY2026E ~52.8%; ~$19.8bn tech budget and AI savings (~$2bn realised) roughly offset volume-driven compensation growth) and provision 6.5% of revenue (~13.8bn; FY2025 was 14,212 = 7.8%, FY2026E ~5.3% is below-trend with card NCOs guided down to ~3.2%; mid-cycle ~6.5-7%). Mature 41.5% = pretax 39.5%: efficiency 53.5% and provision 7.0% as card and wholesale losses normalise and markets revenue mean-reverts. This is ABOVE the FY2018-25 ex-one-off average of ~38.5% by ~1pp, crediting scale, mix shift to fees and AI efficiency, but below FY2026E underlying 42.0%, which sits on a record trading half and a light provision.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~13.5-14% as RWA grows = CET1 capital (~$303bn) / revenue (~1.45x) x RWA growth [4,4,4,3.5,3.5,3,3,3,2.5,2.5]% = ~1.45 x g. FY27: 5.8% of revenue (~$12.3bn, 18% of NPAT retained -> 82% distributed = ~$17.5bn of dividends at $6.60/share + ~$38bn of buybacks, in line with the FY2025 85% payout and the new $50bn authorisation). Steps down with growth to 3.6% at the 2.5% terminal rate (~11% retained -> 89% distributed). No release of the ~$45-55bn excess CET1 is modelled (see book_value_anchor).

bull.growth_rationale: Capital-markets cycle extends (M&A/IPO/issuance keeps building, JPM's ~8.4% IB fee share rises toward 9%), NII compounds 5-6% on deposit share gains and loan growth with the curve steepening, wealth management client assets grow 10%+ on advisor hiring and the JPMD/payments franchise takes wholesale share from stablecoins. Revenue +6% FY27 fading to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 52.0% - provision 6.5% + 2.0 = 43.5. AI-driven productivity (management's ~10% headcount reduction over five years, 1,000 use cases) takes the efficiency ratio to 50.0% by FY30 with credit benign at 7.0% of revenue: 100 - 50.0 - 7.0 + 2.0 = 45.0, held. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$27.6; ROTCE ~24-25%, i.e. the FY2024-26 run-rate sustained, not a new high.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = ~1.45 x RWA growth [5.5,5,5,4.5,4,4,3.5,3.5,3,3]%: faster growth needs more capital even at a better return. FY27 retains 8.0% of revenue (~23% of NPAT); terminal 3% growth retains 4.4% (~12%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: the valuation date sits at a record earnings half, record trading revenue, a below-trend provision, elevated asset prices the CEO himself calls a risk, and ~3.0x tangible book (the top of JPM's 20-year range); a normal credit/markets cycle inside a 10-year horizon is closer to a base rate than a tail. Bull cut to 25%: it needs the capital-markets boom to persist, AI headcount savings to land in full, credit to stay benign and the Basel III final rule to free the excess capital, and the base already credits a mid-cycle margin ~1pp above the FY2018-25 average.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
